content_voiceover: This algorithm addresses management of multiply relapsed myeloma, organizing options by drug class backbone rather than by prior exposure alone, since by this point patients have typically cycled through several drug classes already. Choices should still weigh insurance coverage, patient preference, comorbidities, renal function, neurologic status, hematopoietic reserve, tumor aggressiveness, and extramedullary disease. The anti-CD38 antibody based branch splits into daratumumab, giving DRd, daratumumab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone, DVd, or DKd, and isatuximab, giving isatuximab-Kd or isatuximab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone. The pomalidomide based branch includes Pd, PCd, pomalidomide-Vd, or elotuzumab-Pd. The carfilzomib based branch includes Kd or KCd. The lenalidomide based branch includes IRd or elotuzumab-Rd. And the other category captures clinical trials, compassionate use programs, DCEP, bendamustine, cyclophosphamide, or melphalan combinations, selinexor, allogeneic transplant if appropriate, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T cell therapy. A note on this slide flags that as of 2026, several of these agents, particularly the bispecifics and CAR T products, now have partial reimbursement or expanded insurance coverage that wasn't previously available.
keypoints: Multiple relapse regimens are chosen by drug class backbone, not just prior lines
Anti-CD38 branch splits into daratumumab and isatuximab combinations
Other options include selinexor, allo transplant, bispecifics, and CAR T
By 2026 several novel agents have gained partial reimbursement
keypoint_voiceover: For multiply relapsed disease, organize your thinking around drug class backbones, anti-CD38, pomalidomide, carfilzomib, or lenalidomide based combinations, and know that bispecific antibodies and CAR T cell therapy now sit in the toolbox with expanding reimbursement as of 2026.
